review.summary:
Not safe to treat the F1 fix as closed: the C++ detector rejects the FR hip mid-stroke stall only from the start point that was recorded, and homes it from most other start points (finding V1, high).

**What I ran**
- A native harness around the working-tree `calibration_end_detector.h`, built in the krabby-fwtest image with the repo mounted read-only.
- 239 hip and knee jog moves parsed independently from 25 robot logs, including `clearance-FL-140513` and `clearance-FL-143330`, which the fix stage never saw.
- 77 reconstructions per move: one frame per sample at +0, +0.5 and +0.9 count, two-frame means, a start shifted by one sample either way, a true 50 ms grid at 10 phases and 3 offsets, and 40 random dithers.
- The firmware's own `LegCalibration` class (the `update()` path, loop periods of 1, 2 and 5 ms) driven by a plant that plays the real traces.
- Nothing in the repo was edited, no serial port was opened, nothing was flashed.

**What holds**
- **Fixture:** all 82 real moves in `robot_end_current_replay.hpp` are sample-for-sample identical to my own parse of the logs.
- **Tests:** the detector test file passes 35 of 35 against the working tree (compiled with a small stand-in for Unity).
- **Guards:** removing any one of them makes at least one test fail. I tried eight mutations: the 90%-of-iRef guard, the below-minimum guard, the fallback itself, its normal-sample count, its run bound, its retract current guard, its curl-only limit and the 1000 ms window.
- **Ends at PWM 128 and 150:** all 18 real ends get the right verdict in every reconstruction, and on a 100-point grid of truncation offsets.
- **The recorded FR hip stall:** Stuck in every reconstruction.
- **F2:** every real end at PWM 120 to 150, restarted from every later frame (23,343 replays), is never called Stuck.

**What does not hold**
- **V1 (high):** the FR hip stall is failed as stuck only when the drive starts about 126 to 144 or more edges before the stall point. Started closer, it is homed 878 edges from the real curl end. A retry after the stuck failure starts exactly there.
- **V2 (medium):** real no-signature stalls and real body contacts, replayed as curl drives, are mostly accepted as ends.
- **V3 (medium):** two real limit-switch ends at PWM 120 are within one sample or one count of being called Stuck.
- **V4 (low):** the F1 test and comments claim more than the code does.

The hip-plate note (about 5.5 degrees, top toward the robot's centre) is geometry for the clearance work; it does not enter a trace replay and I did not use it.

Everything is in `C:/Users/nickm/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/78c86551260afdf9/720ce176-f876-4a62-9959-4e2b88a4d5da/scratchpad/ced-verify/trace-replay` (`tools/` for the harnesses and scripts, `out/` for results, `mut/` for the mutated header copies).

Trace: clearance-FR-115750.log move #7 (FRHL at -128 from count -1070, stalls at -878 after 192 edges, current 17-31 against a running level of about 16).

I ran the firmware's own LegCalibration (SEEK at PWM 128) on a plant that plays this trace from the frame matching the hip's distance to the stall point. Nine runs per start distance: loop 1, 2 and 5 ms, current offset +0, +0.5 and +0.9 count.

| Hip starts this many edges before the stall | Result |
|---|---|
| 144-192 | FAIL stuck mid-stroke, 225 of 225 runs |
| 126-142 | stuck in 77 of 81 |
| 114-124 | homed in 48 of 54 |
| 48-112 | `by=switch`, then HOME, 297 of 297 |
| 18-46 | plain stall, then HOME, 135 of 135 |
| 0-16 | no motion, nudge 24 out, curl back 23, then HOME, 81 of 81 |

findings.scenario:
FRHL stalls 878 edges short at PWM 128 and the run fails "stuck mid-stroke". That failure clears the hip's home. The owner retries at 128 with the hip now resting at the stall point: no motion, nudge out 24, curl back 23, accepted, home set 878 edges from the real curl end.

The same happens on a first curl after power-up when the hip rests anywhere within about 125 edges of such a point.

A SEEK-only run then passes with that home. T's hip range [8, 675] maps to 886-1553 real edges, past the body contact at 941-1003 and the extend switch at 1069. A full run only fails later, when the 700-edge sweep presses into the body.
findings.fix:
Do not rest the switch verdict on iRef. In the logs every real limit-switch end is flat: once the count has been still for 3 samples, the current stays within 1 count over 8 samples (22 hip ends, 5 knee switch ends, 26 hip presses). Every retract stall wobbles by 2-7 counts (this trace 5-7). So require a flat, low current for a retract end, including a retract curl's plain Still and the nudge return, and call a stalled, wobbling current Stuck.

I tried a first cut in a scratch copy (tools/flatfix.py, never in the repo). It turned this stall into Stuck from every start (6996 of 6996 direct replays; 147 of 147 LegCalibration runs) and kept every real switch end at 128 and 150 from every start. It is not ready: it flipped the PWM 120 FL knee crawl end of V3 to Stuck, and some hip presses under my dithered reconstructions. It needs a "wait until flat" form and tuning on tenths-resolution data.

Until then, treat a hip home taken after a "stuck mid-stroke" failure, or from a plain stall, as unverified. One option is a re-press at PWM 150 that must not go more than the tolerance deeper.

findings.scenario:
`C 120`, or a day when 128 behaves like 120 (lower battery voltage, cold grease): a healthy FL knee uncurl or FL hip curl fails "stuck mid-stroke" and its home is cleared. It is a nuisance failure, not a wrong home.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute V1. I reproduced it on the C++ in the repo.

**How I tested it.** I wrote my own harness, C:/Users/nickm/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/78c86551260afdf9/720ce176-f876-4a62-9959-4e2b88a4d5da/scratchpad/ced-verify/v1-refute/v1.cpp, with its output in v1.out in the same folder. It includes firmware/arduino/src/actuator/calibration_end_detector.h read-only from the repo and calls `CalibrationEndDetector::sample()` with retract=1, leaving=0 and minStill=1000, which is what leg_calibration.h:747 passes for a SEEK curl. The input is clearance-FR-115750 move #7 (136 samples; the count stops at 191-192 edges; the current climbs to 21-31 and dips to 17 for six frames at samples 101-106). The repo tree is unchanged apart from the untracked .idea/ and parkour pycache.

**Start-distance replays.** For each start, I kept the 37-edge ramp, started the full-PWM tail later, added 3 s of hold at the end, and ran each start three times with current offsets of 0, +0.5 and +0.9 count. The results by total travel to the stall:
- **126-192 edges:** always Stuck (the fixed behaviour).
- **65-122 edges:** Switch in 59 of 60 runs; the one exception, at 117 edges, was Stuck.
  - The detector arms inside the rising-current crawl, so iRef is learned at 189-230 tenths instead of about 161 from the full run.
  - The dip to 170 tenths then passes the slow-arrival rule: 70% of stopRef 250 and 90% of iRef (lines 216-224). The F1 guard therefore does not hold when the drive starts close to the stall.
- **37-63 edges:** the detector never arms and ends Still, the plain-stall rule (lines 343-350).

My breakpoints differ slightly from the reviewer's (48-112 for Switch) because the reconstruction is different, but the pattern is the same.

**Retry path, from the code.** `fail()` (around line 1376) calls `clearHome()`, so a retry starts with the hip unproven. At rest at the stall point there is no motion, so (4c) starts the hip nudge out of 24 edges. The curl back then stalls at the same point. That return is unarmed (fewer than 50 edges), so it ends Still. (4a) accepts it because `driveEdges` is at least CAL_HALL_DETECT_EDGES and it stopped within tolerance of the pre-nudge position. A Stuck failure followed by the obvious retry at 128 therefore homes the hip at the stall point.

**Pre-existing versus new.** The plain-stall and nudge part is the pre-existing, documented limitation ("after a boot an obstacle looks the same"). The 65-122-edge Switch window is the detector itself misclassifying a stall, which is the F1 class the fix stage said it had closed.

**Can it happen on this robot?** This is the only room for downgrading, and it does not refute the finding.
- The one measured hip stall at 128 had the knee 175 counts out. In this tree, SEEK and SWEEP always curl the knee first, and knee-curled hip curls from 700 or less were seen to reach home. A knee-curled stall at 878-1003 has not been measured, so a first-run occurrence in this tree is unproven.
- No measured fact rules it out. FRHL did stall mid-stroke at 128 with rising current, and fr-recover-120231 shows the shortfall depends on position.
- The sequence the owner has already decided on (knee partly uncurled during a full hip sweep, then the hip curls back from about 1069) recreates the F1 configuration exactly.

**Consequence.** The home ends up about 878 edges from the real curl end. A SEEK-only run passes. T and the 700-edge sweep then drive toward the belly contact at 941-1003 and the extend switch at 1069. That is a wrong home, which is high on the rubric.

**Suggested fix direction.** The reviewer's idea is plausible:
- Do not base the switch verdict on an iRef learned near the end.
- Also check that the current is flat and low (for example, near the joint's known switch level, FRHL about 11).
- Do not accept a nudge return or a plain stall as a hip home after a Stuck failure, or treat such a home as unverified.
- Add the later starts of this trace to the fixture with Stuck expected.

**Side note.** The relayed user message, about the hip plate slanting about 5.5 degrees with its top toward the robot's centre, is a geometry fact already in the hardware memory. It has no bearing on V1.

verdict.reasoning:
The mechanism reproduces, but the severity is low, not medium. What it shows is mostly the stall-as-home limit that the docs already state. The part that is new is wording.

How I tested it: I wrote my own parser and harness, independent of the reviewer's tools, in C:/Users/nickm/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/78c86551260afdf9/720ce176-f876-4a62-9959-4e2b88a4d5da/scratchpad/ced-verify/v2-refute/ (ext.py, gen.py, h.cpp, res_a.txt). The harness was compiled in krabby-fwtest against the working-tree calibration_end_detector.h, with the repo mounted read-only. The working tree is identical to HEAD b11cc9ef. I took the four FLKL PWM-80 uncurl stalls from endcur-111808.log (about 96-107 edges each). I resampled them to 50 ms with tenths = 10*int+5, set the ramp as done at k=7, and replayed from every start frame with 12 or more edges left (168 starts per flag set).
- As recorded (retract, leaving): all four full drives end Stuck. The detector does catch the real weak-drive stalls.
- Replayed as a hip curl (retract, not leaving): 85 of 168 accepted (Still 83, Switch 2) and 83 Stuck. Every drive under about 30 edges is an unarmed Still. Armed short-curl fallback Stills still occur at 30-79 edges. Drives of 80 edges or more are all Stuck.
- Replayed as a knee curl (extend): 158 of 168 accepted (Stop 57, Still 101). Every full-length drive ends Stop, e.g. m5 s0 Stop at 96 edges, cur 145/94, because a stall whose current rises 25% matches the knee-stop signature.
So the reviewer's qualitative claims hold on the C++: short curls take any stall as an end, and knee curls take any current-rising stall as an end.

Why the severity is low:
1) The scenario is constructed. The real curls in the same trace reached their ends at PWM 80 (FLKL 107 to 15, FLHL -154 to 0), and 120 and 150 did too. The only real weak stalls are uncurls, which come out Stuck. At the default PWM 128 every end was reached on 2026-11-24. The one real curl stall at 128 (FRHL) is V1's case, not this one. A weak-PWM curl stall needs a non-default PWM below about 110, and SETUP.md line 263 tells the user to calibrate at 128.
2) This is the stall-as-home behaviour the calibration had before the detector. The detector only adds Stuck rejections for long armed drives, so it makes nothing worse. The limit is already disclosed:
   - SETUP.md line 266: "A curl move that moved and then stalled is accepted as the curl end ... after a power-up an obstacle looks the same as the end".
   - SETUP.md line 218: run on the stand.
   - leg_calibration.h header: "after a boot an obstacle looks the same".
   - GLOSSARY: slow drives and short curls are found "by stall alone, as before the end detector".
3) The knee-meets-belly case: SEEK curls the knee first, then the hip. SWEEP curls the knee again with its hip curled, and "ending deeper is accepted and moves a hall home", so a full run corrects it. A SEEK-only run never saves (SETUP.md line 280). It only leaves an in-RAM knee home for that boot, and that home is short of the real stop, which is the safe side.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced the mechanism, but it is not medium. It is a misleading failure message on a run that already fails safely, and it only shows up after a different defect (a wrong hip home). I rate it low.

What I checked:
- I built the working tree's leg_calibration.h in krabby-fwtest:latest against a copy of the reviewer's plant model. The copy and scripts are in C:/Users/nickm/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/78c86551260afdf9/720ce176-f876-4a62-9959-4e2b88a4d5da/scratchpad/ced-verify/r2/ (sim.cpp and run.sh); the repo was mounted read-only.
- In finishMove (leg_calibration.h:1019-1023), endKind_ == Stuck fails StuckMidStroke before the isHallHipSweep / !sweepReached_ SweepShort check at :1029-1035. That ordering is confirmed.
- The hall hip sweep is a +PWM drive. The detector begins with retract = sign_ < 0 = false (:747), so only the extend rule can fire. That rule is speed collapse plus median current >= 125% of iRef. A current drop at a switch never satisfies it, so an extend switch can only end as Stuck.

Sim results on the working tree:
- AF (belly modelled at 941): "END FRHL uncurl hall=62 travel=62 by=stuck cur=256/221", then "FAIL FRHL stuck mid-stroke after 62 edges at PWM 128: raise PWM or check load".
- AX: "by=stuck cur=110/157 ... stuck mid-stroke after 190 edges".
- Healthy run (H): the sweep stops at exactly 700, then "JOINT FRHL min=0 max=700 edges (fixed sweep)" and "PASS_DONE SWEEP saved".

So the reviewer's numbers are real for the model. Why the severity is lower:
1. **It needs a wrong home first.** The sweep counts edges from where the SWEEP curl just ended (startHall_), not from the saved home. To reach the belly at 941, that curl must have stopped at least 241 edges short of the true curl end, which is the R1/F1 defect. In AF the false home comes from the sim's knee-independent force stall at 878. The one measured stall like that (FRHL at 878) happened with the knee 175 out. In calibration the hip only moves with its knee proven curled, and PWM 128 reached every end on 2026-11-24. With a correct home the sweep stops 241 edges short of the belly, so it cannot happen.
2. **The extend-switch case (AX) cannot happen on this robot.** With the knee curled, the tibia meets the belly at 941-1003 counts (FLHL measured) before the hip reaches its extend switch at 1069. AX models no belly, which is not this robot during calibration.
3. **The outcome is safe either way.** The pass fails and the hip is left unhomed (homed=0 in the sim). Nothing is saved, so T can never use a bad range. The detector stops the press within about 1-1.4 s (Stuck rule: 1000 ms window, 400 ms with no forward edge). Which message appears depends on the belly-contact current, which nobody has measured. A clear rise of 125% or more gives Stop, which already reports SweepShort ("obstacle?"). Only a weak rise gives Stuck.
4. **"Raise PWM" is not wrong-headed here.** The only wrong-home mechanism measured on the robot is a force shortfall on the hip curl, and PWM 150 got FRHL home where 128 stalled. A rerun at higher PWM starts with SEEK curling the hip from the belly and should reach the true switch, which fixes the root cause. The reviewer's claim that raising PWM "does not fix the cause" is overstated. The text still misdirects in one sense: the joint is not stuck mid-stroke but blocked, and the operator is not pointed at the home.
5. **The documentation gap is real but text-only.** The detector header line 47 ("extend (+PWM, a mechanical stop)") and docs/GLOSSARY.md "Limit-switch end" both omit that the hip's extended end is also a limit switch.

Verdict: not refuted. The code path is real and reproducible, but it is low severity: a diagnostic message plus a doc gap behind another defect, with a safe fail and nothing saved. The suggested fix is cheap and reasonable as a polish item: report a hall hip sweep that ends before 700 edges (any end kind) as SweepShort with "check its home", and fix the header and glossary text.

The relayed user note (the hip plate slants about 5.5 degrees, top toward the centre) is already in the hardware memory. It does not affect this finding.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this against the working-tree C++. I did not rely on the reviewer's run. My harness is C:/Users/nickm/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/78c86551260afdf9/720ce176-f876-4a62-9959-4e2b88a4d5da/scratchpad/ced-verify/r3-semantics/sim.cpp with run.sh beside it. It started from the reviewer's plant model in ced-verify/robot-run. I built and ran it in krabby-fwtest with the repo mounted read-only, and changed nothing in the repo.

**The code path**
- legCalibrationStep (leg_calibration.h:375-381) makes SEEK knee curl then hip curl, nothing more.
- After a boot the knee is not homed, so proven is false. The first curl goes through branch (4c) at about lines 1145-1157: if it moved, it calls accept(..., Hall && !proven) and sets the home where the drive stopped. Nothing checks it against the saved stroke or the hip position. The header comment admits this: "after a boot an obstacle looks the same".
- The end detector's extend rule (speed below 25% of vRef and current at or above 125% of iRef) has no position term, so it cannot tell a blocked curl from the leg's own stop.

**The runs**
- I made the obstacle exist only while the hip is at 941 or more, as on the robot (scenario K2: hip resting at 1069, knee 400 out, belly contact 150 short of the knee's stop).
- Curl only (SEEK): 'END FRKL curl hall=-151 travel=249 by=stop', 'HOME FRKL count=151', then the hip curls to its switch and the pass completes with no warning. The knee home is 151 edges toward uncurl. K3 (contact 60 short) homes 61 short the same way.
- Full run (SEEK+SWEEP): SWEEP step 0 re-curls with the hip curled, giving 'WARN FRKL home moved 150 edges' and 'HOME FRKL count=1', then stores the correct -784..0. So only Curl only is exposed, as the reviewer said.

**Can it happen on this robot?**
- The measured facts say yes. A curled knee meets the belly at hip 941-1003.
- The knee 164 counts out clears the belly over the full hip stroke, and the owner ran exactly that pose (hip 1069, knee 157/164) in the clearance tests. So the knee can sit past the contact zone while the hip is extended.
- Opening the port resets FRONT, so hall counts restart even without a power cycle.
- The GUI makes Curl only the routine step after every power-up.
- The one thing not measured: the knee pushing into the belly has never been recorded. If that contact gives no current rise, it would end by=stuck and fail the pass, which is safe. The leg stop and the hip-into-belly contact are both load-rising stalls, so by=stop is the likely outcome.

**Consequences, checked in actuator_manager.h**
- T clamps the knee to [minStop+8, maxStop-25] from the saved stroke, with no check against the home.
- With the home d edges short, every knee target sits d edges more uncurled than commanded. The lower bound is d-8 edges past the real uncurl switch, so the switch stops the rod and the T stall guard trips.
- The upper bound is d+25 short of the real stop, which is safe.
- The range guard (60-edge margin at line 405) only catches this if the knee is later jogged deeper than its home by more than 60. T never does that, so the wrong home stays silent.

**Severity: high under the stated rubric.** The robot homes a joint at a wrong position, by up to about 150 edges (about 28 mm of rod, a large knee angle), with no warning. T's lower bound also goes past a real limit.

It needs a hip parked beyond T's range (above 675, reachable only by manual jogs or test scripts) at a reset, and a knee uncurled past the contact zone. Damage potential is limited, because the error is toward uncurl and the limit switch catches the low end. A reviewer weighing likelihood could call it medium. It is still a real, unwarned wrong home on the routine homing path.

The suggested fix works on the C++ path: re-curl the knee after its hip curl in SEEK. That curl runs proven, so it reaches the same 'home moved' branch the full run already uses. A cheaper alternative is to warn when a knee's first SEEK curl ends by=stop before its hip is proven curled.

The user's note that the hip plate slants about 5.5 degrees is already in the hardware memory and does not change this conclusion.

synth.verdict: Not ready to flash and calibrate. Two confirmed high findings can each home a joint at the wrong position with no warning. V1/R1: a hip that stalls mid-stroke for lack of force is still homed at the stall point when its curl starts within about 110-125 edges of that point, including the obvious rerun at 128 after a "stuck mid-stroke" failure. R3: Curl only can home a knee against the belly. Pushing the tree to the feature branch is fine.
confirmed: HIGH - V1 = R1 (same defect, found independently by both reviews and reproduced by both verifiers): the F1 fix only holds when the hip curl reaches running speed before the stall. On the real FRHL stall trace (clearance-FR-115750 #7), drives of 126-192 edges end Stuck. Drives of about 36-122 edges end Switch: iRef is learned in the slowdown, so the dip to 17 passes the 90%-of-iRef guard. Shorter drives never arm and end as a plain Still with no current check. fail() clears the home, so a rerun at 128 from the stall point nudges out 24, curls back, and homes about 878 edges short. T's hip range [8,675] then reaches real 886-1553 edges, past the belly contact (941-1003) and the extend switch (1069), and the 1560 range guard never fires. Fix: before homing on any retract curl (Switch, plain Still, nudge return), require the limit-switch signature, a flat current at or below the switch-open level (per joint, or relative to the first full-PWM samples). Learn the slow-arrival reference before the slowdown. Keep the last proven home through fail(), so a rerun that ends far from it fails instead of re-homing. Change SETUP.md so a hip that fails stuck at 128 is not rerun at 128. Add all 117 later-start cuts and the nudge-return case to the fixture as Stuck.

HIGH (verifier raised it from medium) - R3: Curl only (SEEK) curls each knee before its hip and never curls the knee again. After a reset with the hip parked at 941 or more and the knee out past the contact zone, the knee stops on the belly (by=stop, which looks the same as the leg stop) and is homed up to about 150 edges short. T's lower bound then runs past the uncurl switch. A full run corrects this in SWEEP; Curl only does not. Fix: make SEEK per leg knee curl, hip curl, knee curl again (the second curl is proven and re-homes through 'home moved'), or at least warn when the first knee curl ends by=stop before its hip is proven.

MEDIUM - V3: two real limit-switch ends at PWM 120 (FLKL uncurl endcur-111808 #10, FLHL curl #17) are one sample or one count from 'stuck mid-stroke'. #10 passes only because of a one-frame hall blip. Result: a nuisance failure and a cleared home, never a wrong home. PWM 128 has margin on every recorded end. Fix: do not let Stuck fire while a switch-drop test is pending or the current is still falling (or lengthen the retract stillness to 500-600 ms). Measure arrival speed over the last few edges, not at the single last-edge sample. Add the blip-removed #10 and the one-sample-late #17 to the fixture. Correct the 'an edge at least every 0.3 s' comment.

LOW (verifier lowered it from medium) - V2: short curls, weak-PWM curls and all knee curls take any stall as an end (a knee takes any stall where the current rises 25%). This is the documented behaviour from before the detector, and the cases are constructed. Fix: correct the header lines 49-59, GLOSSARY:64 and the commit text so they say 'stuck mid-stroke' only protects long armed drives. Raising CAL_PWM_MIN closes the weak-PWM path.

LOW (verifier lowered it from medium) - R2: a hall hip sweep that hits the body or the extend switch fails as 'stuck mid-stroke: raise PWM', because Stuck is checked before SweepShort. It needs a wrong home first, the run fails safely and nothing is saved. Fix: report any hip sweep that ends short of 700 as SweepShort with 'check its home', and state in the header and glossary that the hip's extended end is also a limit switch.

LOW (not verified) - R4: a blind hip nudge runs at the full calibration PWM for 2 s with the knee curled and can press the tibia into the belly. It needs a dead hall. Fix: cap the hip nudge PWM like the knee's, or cut the no-edge nudge to about 1 s.

LOW (not verified) - R5 / V4: SETUP.md:264/343, GLOSSARY, the GUI help, the F1 test comment and header lines 49-51 claim a mid-stroke stall is never taken as an end. Fix: reword to the measured bound (Stuck only after about 130 or more edges of free running), and give a hip-specific recovery (jog home or run at 150).
refuted: Nothing was fully refuted. Partly refuted: V3(a)'s 'Stuck in 30 of 30 on a true 50 ms grid' did not reproduce. The verifier's time-based grids keep the hall blip and give Switch 30/30, so that end depends on one jitter count, not on how it is sampled.

V2 severity: refuted as medium. The scenarios are constructed, behave as before the detector, are documented, and need a non-default PWM below about 110. V2(c), the real knee curl 23 edges shallower, is inside the 40-edge tolerance and is not evidence.

R2 severity and the claim that raising PWM 'does not fix the cause': refuted as medium. It only follows a wrong home, nothing is saved, the AX case (extend switch with no belly) cannot happen with the knee curled, and a rerun at 150 does reach the true switch.

F4: CAL_PWM_MIN 40 or about 110. Raising it removes the weak-drive paths in V2, V3 and R5 (PWM 80 stalls with no current signature), so about 110 is recommended.

New - V1/R1 fix design: a per-joint switch-open current ceiling (FL 7-8, FRHL 11) or a relative 'flat and low' test (the reviewer's scratch flatfix flipped a PWM-120 crawl end and needs tuning on tenths data). Also decide whether fail() keeps the last proven hall home as a reference.
New - R3: add a third SEEK step (knee curl again after the hip is curled; costs time on every Curl only) or only warn.
New - R4: add a hip nudge PWM cap, and its value.

New - interim robot procedure if a supervised run happens before the fix: jog every hip inside 0-700 and every knee curled before reset or calibration. Never rerun at 128 after a hip 'stuck mid-stroke'; jog it home or use PWM 150. Watch for any hip HOME without by=switch.
synth.summary: Both reviews independently found that the F1 fix is incomplete (V1 = R1, high, reproduced by both verifiers on the working-tree C++). A force-shortfall hip stall is homed as a switch or plain stall whenever the curl starts within about 110-125 edges of it, including the natural rerun after a stuck failure. That leaves T driving the hip into the belly and past the extend switch with no guard. R3 (high after verification) lets Curl only home a knee on the belly. V3 is a real medium nuisance at PWM 120. V2, R2, R4, R5 and V4 are low (wording, caps, message order). Nothing was refuted outright; only some severities and one resampling claim fell. Gates are green and the push can go ahead, but do not flash or calibrate until V1/R1 is fixed, preferably with a switch-open current check on retract homes and a kept last home, and R3 is fixed or warned on. The 5.5-degree hip-plate slant (top toward the centre) does not change any finding: the belly-contact limits are measured hall counts. It belongs to the clearance work.
